title: Workspace Traverse: compact handoff & navigation IA redesign
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: The current Console sidebar and workspace switcher create frequent context loss for users who operate across multiple projects and need quick cost and rollout signals. Goal: create a compact, low-height handoff panel anchored to the left rail that surfaces workspace context, per-workspace cost lenses, and rollout state without blowing up vertical space. Deliver a hi-fidelity prototype, engineering handoff spec, and an A/B rollout plan tied to Console telemetry.
background: Research from Dec–Jan interviews (internal product teams + 3 beta customers) showed repeated friction when switching workspaces: users lose quick access to in-flight rollouts and cost breakdowns, and the existing global switcher forces a full page navigation. The Console is increasingly used for rapid triage; we need a more ambient context layer that surfaces time-sensitive signals (rollout status, cost spikes) and keeps a smaller persistent footprint.
goals: Reduce workspace switch latency (perceived) by keeping context visible
Surface per-workspace cost summary and alerts in the rail with 1-click drill-in
Expose rollout state (canary/failed/healthy) at glance and provide quick rollback link
Keep vertical real-estate usage under 64px when compacted and expandable to 200px on hover/peek
constraints: Must fit within existing left-rail CSS grid and accessibility patterns
Behavior must degrade gracefully on narrow viewports and mobile
Engineering depends on runtime breadcrumbs (ENG-2119) and routing shim (ENG-3176)
Telemetry events must be instrumented (PM-402) before rollout
proposed_solution_summary: Introduce a compact ‘handoff strip’ at the top of the left rail that shows current workspace chip, small sparkline cost, and a rollout pill. Clicking the chip opens a full overlay workspace switcher; hovering the strip expands to reveal quick actions: View cost, View rollouts, Switch workspace, and Recent traces. The strip uses color-coded rollout states and an affordance for immediate rollback where user has permission.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype with desktop & narrow width states linked in artifacts
Design tokens and component spec for handoff strip published to the design system
Edge-case flows documented: permissioned rollback, multiple concurrent rollouts, offline state
A/B plan with success metrics: 10% reduction in workspace switch time, 15% increase in quick-rollout actions for power users
Engineering sign-off on feasibility and perf impact notes from infra team
decisions: Opted for persistent compact strip (vs modal-first approach) to minimize navigation disruption
Rollout pill will be color-coded (green/amber/red) and include textual status on hover to keep info accessible
Cost overview will be an aggregated sparkline + top-line value; deep breakdown opens Console cost page to avoid duplication
Rollback CTA surface will only appear for users with policy permission (RBAC check) handled server-side
tradeoffs: Pros: ambient context reduces navigation overhead and surfaces critical signals faster
Cons: additional visual density in the rail — mitigated by compact collapse state
Engineering cost: requires lightweight telemetry and routing guards; will add ~1.5% to initial left-rail render time unless cached
